subject: Clarification: log preservation, evidence export, and data residency after incident
messages:
From: Sarah Lambert <sarah.lambert@acme-analytics.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Log retention & evidence preservation after Friday's incident

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the quick post-mortem on Friday. Our security team has a few follow-ups around evidence preservation and what you can provide for our internal forensics:

- Which log types can Redwood export on request (request logs, inference traces, audit trail, host-level system logs)?
- Current retention windows for hosted customers in US and EU regions; can you place a legal hold to preserve beyond the standard window?
- Do you provide cryptographic hashes/manifests and an auditable chain-of-custody for exported artifacts?
- Any constraints on sharing raw request payloads (we may need prompt/request payloads for root-cause analysis and to search for PII exposure)?

I've attached our standard chain-of-custody template for reference. Please let me know what you can share and what paperwork (DPA amendment / letter request / subpoena) would be required if there are restrictions.

We'd like to avoid a protracted evidence collection; a clear checklist from your side would help.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lambert
Security Operations
Acme Analytics

Attachment: Acme_chain_of_custody_template.docx
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lambert <sarah.lambert@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Log retention & evidence preservation after Friday's incident

Sarah —

Appreciate the note and the template. High-level answers up front and we can iterate on specifics in a quick call:

1) Exportable artifacts: request-level logs (timestamp, model id, response tokens counts, request metadata), inference traces (where enabled), platform audit logs (user actions, API keys usage), and service-level metrics. Host-level OS logs are available for Dedicated/Private deployments only; hosted customers have limited host-level access.

2) Retention: default hosted retention is 30 days for request logs and 90 days for audit logs. EU-hosted data is kept in EU regions; we can export region-scoped artifacts. We can put accounts on a temporary preservation window (up to 90 days) with product ops approval.

3) Chain-of-custody: we produce an export manifest and a SHA256 checksum for each exported artifact; exports are delivered via a signed S3 URL with KMS encryption. We can also generate a custody.pdf that lists transfer timestamps and operator IDs.

4) Raw payloads: raw request payloads may include customer-provided data and any PII in prompts. We need a written request describing scope and legal basis; our legal team will advise on redaction or secure transfer.

Next steps: Vivek (cc'd) will outline the exact artifacts and export formats, and Laura (cc'd) will confirm the legal controls. Happy to book a 30-min slot tomorrow to walk through the checklist.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-log-export-guidance.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Lambert <sarah.lambert@acme-analytics.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Log retention & evidence preservation after Friday's incident

Hi all —

Putting the technical baseline here so Acme's SOC has a concrete checklist. This is what we can reliably provide for hosted customers (subject to legal/contract limits):

- API request logs: JSONL export with timestamp, request_id, model_version, tokens_in/out, latency, origin region. Default retention: 30 days; can extend to 90 days on request for preservation.
- Inference traces / generation deltas: available if tracing was enabled for the workspace; otherwise not captured retroactively.
- Platform audit logs: all console/API user actions, retention 90 days.
- KV-cache internal metadata: not part of exports (we do not export raw KV caches).
- Host system/hypervisor logs: only for Dedicated/Private customers; not accessible for standard hosted tenants.

Forensics & chain-of-custody process (standard):
- We create a manifest.csv listing each exported file, its SHA256 hash, size, and export timestamp.
- Exports staged to a customer-specific S3 bucket in the requested region; links are time-limited and encrypted with the customer's KMS (if configured) or Redwood-managed KMS.
- A human-signed custody record (PDF) is produced that logs operator id, action timestamp, and export job id.
- We can timestamp and notarize manifest via our internal audit system; if Acme needs third-party notarization we can coordinate but that will add time.

Notes on PII/raw payloads:
- We do not automatically redact request payloads before export. If payloads may contain PII, we require a written scoping request and the customer's Acknowledgement of Data Handling (we can provide a template). For regulated workloads we advise using Dedicated/Private deployments next time.

I'll open a ticket (JIRA INF-7421) to track the export job and will attach the manifest once the export completes.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Related link: https://redwood-internal.company/forensics/playbook/2026
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Log retention & evidence preservation after Friday's incident

Sarah —

Quick legal note: providing raw request payloads to third parties can trigger data processing obligations under Acme's own policies and under applicable DPAs. Operationally we can provide payload exports for troubleshooting, but:

- We need a written scoping statement from Acme describing the timeframe and a risk assessment for PII exposure.
- If Acme requires us to process or transform payloads beyond simple export (e.g., redaction, tokenization), we'll need a DPA amendment and signing authority from Acme's legal.
- For litigation or formal investigations, please work with your counsel; we will respond to subpoenas and lawful process per our policy.

I'll prepare a short template scoping statement and a one-page checklist for the DPA amendment. If you can confirm the exact date range and whether you want raw payloads or redacted extracts, we can expedite.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
